text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Residents of Zimbabwe's southern city of Bulawayo have urged President Robert Mugabe to facilitate government compensation packages for victims of the Fifth Brigade atrocities in the Matebeleland and Midlands provinces during the 1980s.

- A consortium of six local businessmen have formed a television broadcasting company which is understood to be planning a takeover of the state-owned Zimbabwe Broadcasting Corporation's second televison channel and it's fourth radio station.

- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe's plans to undertake a Z$200 million computerisation programme have been sent back to the drawing board after technical experts advised that the chosen firm did not fully meet the needs of the bank.

- Zimbabwean vice president Simon Muzenda has urged Southern African countries to actively pursue the formation of an economic bloc if the region is to survive the challenges posed by other regional groupings worldwide.
- South Africa's President Nelson Mandela is expected in Zimbabwe on Monday on a three-day state visit at the end of which he will attend the World Economic Forum.

- Police have mounted an intensive manhunt for escaped prisoner Edgar Masendeke who is wanted for murder, attempted murder and armed robbery. He has also committed abductions, rape and robberies since breaking out of remand prison two years ago.
